parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a federal binary-sex executive order (bar on X markers, facility exclusion in federally funded single-sex spaces, a Feb 2025 consular cable telling officers to refuse cases with sex-discrepancy doubt and consider a lifetime fraud bar) with this division's March 2025 binary-statute covering bathrooms, locker rooms, shelters, dorms and prisons, a documented trans woman's trespass arrest and 24-hour men's-ward detention, no statewide gender-identity discrimination protection, and a religious-refusal statute with qualified immunity. A federal hate-crime statute, employment protection, functioning courts blocking several orders, and no documented execution or imprisonment regime keep this out of the low bands; tier-1 facility exclusion plus border refusal risk keeps it out of Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and consideration of a lifetime ineligibility fraud finding; X markers barred; documented passport blocks and advisories from 8+ foreign governments.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; litigation pending; existing X passports valid until expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal → fraud allegation → lifetime ineligibility; division document rules do not touch a foreign passport but signal official culture.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest of a trans woman under a bathroom/trespass law, held 24 hours in a men's ward; statute reaches prisons and shelters; federal immigration custody reports of beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; conversion-therapy-style federal prison policy from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; no prosecution documented under the March 2025 statute; no capital exposure.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility ban → asked to leave → trespass charge → birth-sex custody placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division statute defines only male/female and covers locker rooms, bathrooms, rape-crisis centres, dormitories, prisons; federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; 9+ units ban facilities in all government buildings; 4 units criminalise in some circumstances; state rated in 'Worst' tier.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban; genital-examination language was struck before signing; some units affirmatively protect.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor meets this at rest stops, parks, courthouses, shelters and transit — unavoidable once visible.

care_services.exposure: Minors' care banned except severe dysphoria diagnosed by two physicians; adult public-insurance exclusion upheld by an appeals court in 2026; federal funding restrictions and youth-record subpoenas.
care_services.protection: No documented ban on out-of-pocket or emergency care for adult visitors; adult exclusion challenge argued Dec 2025 and unresolved; earlier ban ruled unconstitutional in 2022.
care_services.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor risks care denial and outing at the point of treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; executive order labels minor care 'mutilation'; 66% poll support for binary document markers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states the reward is not conditioned on gender ideology; strategy says powers will not target mere disagreement; national employment and hate-crime statutes cover gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises the climate of outing and hostility without itself operating against an individual visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: April 2025 bill requiring teachers to out trans, non-binary and intersex students passed both houses awaiting gubernatorial action (final status unresolved); Jan 2025 order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; school facility bans; minors' care ban.
minors_guardians.protection: Outing bill not confirmed enacted; no documented prosecution of a visiting parent or guardian; no documented penalty for a travelling family as such.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family trip → clinic or facility encounter → state inquiry or denied care for the child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific street violence rate or pattern against visitors. National statistics break out bias by sexual orientation (one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias incidents), not gender identity, and give no denominator for visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; only 23 units add state-level coverage; 15 cities bar gender-identity discrimination including public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Unknown — neither a documented pattern nor documented protective enforcement for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Religious-refusal statute grants qualified immunity for service denial on gender identity; athletics case, outing bill, ordinance-nullification bill and adult coverage challenge all unresolved; facility-ban map page returns 404; enforcement patterns unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several federal orders; ACLU suit over passport markers proceeds; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules; 15 city ordinances and national employment/hate-crime law operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but their availability depends on which provision is in force and where in the division the traveller is.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far below this case: Saruth detains trans visitors in crowded cells with tolerated assaults, withheld medical care and delayed habeas hearings, with capital echoes. Here there is no custody regime routinely triggered by being trans, no documented pattern of violence in detention for visitors, and courts actively enjoin hostile measures — so this rating sits well above the 0.15 tier.

Closest analogue: routine exposure at checkpoints and everyday services, official discretion producing detention and denial of care, only a narrow and slow remedy. This dossier is somewhat worse — it adds a documented trespass arrest with men's-ward detention, a statute expressly reaching shelters and crisis centres, and a border cable contemplating lifetime ineligibility — hence slightly below 0.45.

Far above this case: Vessalia's equality law covers gender identity in services, officers are trained and disciplined, and remedies produce apologies and compensation. Here the operative statutes exclude rather than protect, no statewide discrimination cover exists, and a service refusal enjoys statutory immunity — structurally the opposite of the 0.85 tier.

Somewhat above this case: Kestrel Isles' exposure is discretionary secondary screening with administrative refusal and slow-but-real appeal, no facility or custody regime. This dossier combines similar border discretion with a standing binary facility statute, documented arrest, and religious-refusal immunity, justifying a score a notch lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one system with two enforcers. At the border, the Feb 2025 cable converts any document-presentation discrepancy into a discretionary refusal and a possible lifetime fraud finding — severe and traveller-specific, though never automatic and under litigation. Inside, both the federal order and the division's binary statute strip trans people from gender-congruent facilities across rest stops, shelters, dorms and prisons; the trespass offence requires refusal to leave, but a trans woman's arrest and men's-ward detention show the chain from exclusion to custody is real. Layered on top: no statewide discrimination protection, religious-refusal immunity for service denials, restricted minor care, and an unresolved outing bill. Mitigation is genuine but partial — functioning courts enjoining orders, a federal hate-crime statute, employment protection, 15 protective cities, and no documented killing or imprisonment regime. Net: consistent, structural exposure without catastrophic severity — Elevated Risk.
